gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hie: Warnes goes bold and expressive, every stroke cut to a single width and tapering off before it touches its neighbor. And Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs follows in sans-serif form, modern and neutral, so the heading gets to be loud when it's big and short.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Noto Sans Arabic reads clean and modern, with wide openings on its small letters and a pronounced x-height. Warnes is the showman, its bowls never swelling, while the body font quietly does the everyday carrying.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Noto Sans Armenian feels approachable and businesslike, with rounded letters that open wide. Warnes brings the spectacle, its round bowls outlined without any swelling or thinning, while the body font stays on task with its full, generous lowercase c, s and z.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Warnes is expressive and bold, with tails and terminals as thick as its main stems. Noto Sans Avestan counters with curves whose tips never touch and a pronounced x-height, which makes the whole pair feel modern.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Expressive from the first glance, Warnes keeps its lowercase n arch and stem matching, with wide-spaced letters. And Noto Sans Balinese settles in underneath with short ascenders and a breathing space inside every curve, so the page feels modern rather than crowded.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Wire-bent and loud, with almost no stroke contrast in Warnes. Noto Sans Bamum is the pair's strongest card, its curved strokes ending before they turn inward and its counters wide open in every small letter.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-batak: Noto Sans Batak stands chunky like a carpenter's pencil stroke. Over a long page it stays approachable, its wide-open e never looking squeezed shut, while Warnes keeps its heading strokes at a unit width throughout and saves the bold stretched swagger for the top.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Contemporary in feel, Warnes looks like glass-tube lettering, hollow and constant in thickness, while Noto Sans Bengali sits below it in sans-serif form. Capitals barely rise above the lowercase there, which quiets the page.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-carian: Noto Sans Carian reads professional and clean, its terminals staying apart like open scissor blades and tiny gaps cutting in under the ascender tops. Warnes sits above it as a flat, unswelling line along every curve.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-cham: Noto Sans Cham opens with generous entry space in its c shapes and rounded, lofty lowercase forms. Warnes looks wire-bent across the whole word, and Noto Sans Cham gives a long passage a modern, clean steadiness beneath it.
